notable_absence.finding: None of the roughly 40 Service-object parameters or the 3 Node-object parameters carries an edition gate or version-availability citation - the same absence round 21's analytics/config.json already found on the prose management page, now confirmed on the REST reference schema itself, which lists defaults, minimums and maximums for many parameters (e.g. dcpBufferAckWatermark: Minimum 1, Maximum 100) but never a version or edition.

cross_component_finding: This page's Security section names a three-role disjunction (Full Admin, Cluster Admin, Analytics Admin) for the 'Analytics Manage' scheme gating both config endpoints, distinct from and narrower than analytics-rest-service/index.md's (this batch) six-role list for the query endpoint's 'Analytics Manage / Analytics Select' scheme - the same security-scheme name ('Analytics Manage') is reused across two REST references in this batch with two different concrete role sets, confirming role requirements are genuinely per-endpoint rather than uniform across the Analytics REST surface.
cross_product_finding: No Capella-specific content appears on this page. Node-level JVM and storage tuning parameters (jvmArgs, storageBuffercacheSize, compilerFramesize, etc.) are stated to be exposed by cbcollect_info and the System Event log - both on-premises Server administrative mechanisms with no stated Capella equivalent, consistent with round 21's appendix_5_python.json finding that Capella customers lack node-level administrative access.
